rows.speaker: الفراء وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: They gloss ghāsiq as night when its darkness thickens; related uses describe an eye full of tears or a wound full of blood, and Ibn Qays’s verse witnesses nightfall.
rows.anchor: أن الغاسق هو اليل إذا عظم ظلامه من قوله

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says ghāsiq means cold; night is called ghāsiq because it is colder than daytime, and the word is associated with zamharīr.
rows.anchor: الغاسق في اللغة هو البارد ، وسمي الليل غاسقا لأنه أبرد من النهار

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some take ghāsiq and ghassāq as something flowing, from an eye flowing with water; night is named for darkness pouring over the earth.
rows.anchor: الغاسق والغساق هو السائل من قولهم : غسقت العين تغسق غسقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wuqūb is entry into something else until hidden from sight; waqbah is a hollow that water enters, and īqāb means putting something into it.
rows.anchor: أما الوقوب فهو الدخول في شيء آخر بحيث يغيب عن العين

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Many exegetes identify the ghāsiq as night entering; its dangers include emerging predators and vermin, assault, theft, fire, and little chance of rescue.
rows.anchor: أن الغاسق إذا وقب هو الليل إذا دخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites a legal ruling: if someone attacked at night draws a weapon and is killed by the person attacked, qisas is not due; the daytime case incurs qisas because help is available.
rows.anchor: ولو كان نهارا يلزمه لأنه يوجد فيه الغوث

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some say harmful spirits, identified as jinn and devils, spread at night because sunlight seems to overpower them, while night gives them a degree of dominance.
rows.anchor: إن في الليل تنتشر الأرواح المؤذية المسماة بالجن والشياطين

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba identifies ghāsiq as the moon, named for eclipsing, when its light vanishes and it darkens; wuqūb is entering that darkening.
rows.anchor: الغاسق القمر سمي به لأنه يكسف فيغسق

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: A report from ʿĀʾisha says the Prophet took her hand, pointed at the moon, and told her to seek refuge from its evil as the ghāsiq when it enters.
rows.anchor: روى أبو سلمة عن عائشة أنه أخذ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بيدها

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba explains the command in the report as seeking refuge from the moon when it enters an eclipse.
rows.anchor: تعوذي بالله من شره إذا وقب أي إذا دخل في الكسوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī offers another lunar reading: the moon is dark in itself, hence ghāsiq, and wuqūb is the disappearance of its light at the month’s end.
rows.anchor: وهو أنه صح أن القمر في جرمه غير مستنير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī reports astrologers’ claim that the moon is inauspicious and weak at month’s end as its light wanes; sorcerers then practice magic said to cause illness.
rows.anchor: إنه في آخر الشهر يكون منحوسا قليل القوة لأنه لا يزال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says that lunar timing fits the revelation occasion, since the sūra was revealed because they bewitched the Prophet to make him ill.
rows.anchor: وهذا مناسب لسبب نزول السورة فإنها إنما نزلت لأجل أنهم سحروا النبي

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the ghāsiq as the Pleiades when they set; illnesses increase when they fall and recede when they rise.
rows.anchor: وكانت الأسقام تكثر عند وقوعها

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: In Ibn Zayd’s reading, the Pleiades are ghāsiq because they pour down in setting westward, and wuqūb is their going beneath the earth and vanishing.
rows.anchor: لانصبابه عند وقوعه في المغرب

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: The author of al-Kashshāf allows ghāsiq to mean a black snake and wuqūb its strike or puncture, treating waqb and naqb as equivalent.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يراد بالغاسق الأسود من الحيات ووقوبه ضربة ونقبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī judges the black-snake interpretation the weakest of the proposed explanations.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن هذا التأويل أضعف الوجوه المذكورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation takes the ghāsiq as the sun when it sets: its motion through the sphere is called ghasaq, and wuqūb is its disappearance beneath the earth.
rows.anchor: هو الشمس إذا غابت وإنما سميت غاسقا لأنها في الفلك تسبح

none: Only a heading and verse text.

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf’s author defines nafth as blowing with a trace of saliva; others define it as blowing alone.
rows.anchor: أن النفث النفخ مع ريق

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet is quoted saying that Gabriel blew into his heart, illustrating nafth.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من قال : إنه النفخ فقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural of knot evokes a sorcerer reciting an incantation while repeatedly tying a thread and blowing on each knot.
rows.anchor: أن الساحر إذا أخذ في قراءة الرقية أخذ خيطا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation uses the feminine form because women were known for the practice; Rāzī says binding hearts, resolve, and imagination supposedly made their work stronger given their lesser learning and stronger desires.
rows.anchor: أن هذه الصناعة إنما تعرف بالنساء لأنهن يعقدن وينفثن

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda identifies the female blowers as the daughters of the Jewish Labīd ibn al-Aʿṣam, who bewitched the Prophet.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة : { النفاثات } هن بنات لبيد بن أعصم اليهودي

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes al-naffāthāt to mean souls.
rows.anchor: المراد من : { النفاثات } النفوس

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: A third interpretation takes al-naffāthāt as groups: the more sorcerers join in one act, the stronger its effect.
rows.anchor: المراد منها الجماعات ، وذلك لأنه كلما كان اجتماع السحرة

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim reads the phrase as women acting upon knots in men’s convictions and opinions, metaphorically loosening their resolve as saliva loosens a rope knot.
rows.anchor: وهو اختيار أبي مسلم : { من شر النفاثات } أي النساء في العقد

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: On this reading, women’s strong place in men’s hearts lets them change men from one opinion and determination to another; the Prophet is told to seek refuge from this harm.
rows.anchor: فمعنى الآية أن النساء لأجل كثرة حبهن في قلوب الرجال يتصرفن في الرجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī calls Abū Muslim’s interpretation good, while acknowledging that it conflicts with the majority of exegetes.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن هذا القول حسن ، لولا أنه على خلاف قول أكثر المفسرين

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilites deny that magic has effects and explain seeking refuge from the women as refuge from the sin of their magic.
rows.anchor: أنكرت المعتزلة تأثير السحر

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilites also say refuge is sought from women’s use of magic to tempt people.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أن يستعاذ من فتنتهن الناس بسحرهن

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: A third Muʿtazilite explanation is protection from women feeding people poor-quality foods that cause insanity or death.
rows.anchor: والثالث : أن يستعاذ من إطعامهن الأطعمة الرديئة المورثة للجنون والموت

none: Only a heading and verse text.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An envier intensely wants another person’s blessing removed for himself and would use any available scheme to do it; therefore God commands seeking refuge from him.
rows.anchor: أن الحاسد هو الذي تشتد محبته لإزالة نعمة الغير إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This sūra encompasses every evil against which one seeks protection in religion and worldly life.
rows.anchor: وقد دخل في هذه السورة كل شر يتوفى ويتحرز منه دينا ودينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says the Prophet rejoiced when this sūra was revealed because it and the following sūra together seek refuge from every matter.
rows.anchor: لما نزلت فرح رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بنزولها لكونها مع ما يليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evil of an envier can also mean his sin and repugnant state while envying, along with the manifestation of its effect.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد بشر الحاسد إثمه وسماجة حاله في وقت حسده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although “evil of what He created” is universal, the specified threats are named to signal that they are among the greatest kinds of evil.
rows.anchor: تنبيها على أن هذه الشرور أعظم أنواع الشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blowers are definite because every such blower is evil; ghāsiq and envier are indefinite because not every dark thing or envier is evil, and envy for good can be praiseworthy.
rows.anchor: عرف النفاثات لأن كل نفاثة شريرة ، ونكر غاسقا لأنه ليس كل غاسق شريرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī identifies Sūrat al-Nās as Medinan and consisting of six verses.
rows.anchor: وهي ست آيات مدنية

rows.speaker: قرىء
rows.claim: A reading omits the hamza in qul aʿūdhu and transfers its vowel to the lām, as in fa-khudh arbaʿatan min al-ṭayr.
rows.anchor: قرىء : { قل أعوذ } بحذف الهمزة ونقل حركتها إلى اللام

rows.speaker: القراء
rows.claim: All readers agree not to apply imāla to al-nās; al-Kisāʾī is reported to apply it when the word is genitive.
rows.anchor: وأيضا أجمع القراء على ترك الإمالة في الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although God is Lord of all created things, He is specified here as Lord of people because the refuge is from a whisperer in people’s breasts: people appeal to their Lord, ruler, and protector.
rows.anchor: أن الاستعاذة وقعت من شر الموسوس في صدور الناس فكأنه قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reason for specifying people is that they are the noblest creatures in the world.
rows.anchor: أن أشرف المخلوقات في العالم هم الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the person commanded to seek refuge is human, reciting the verse is like saying, “my Lord, my King, my God.”
rows.anchor: فإذا قرأ الإنسان هذه صار كأنه يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī treats “King of people” and “God of people” as explanatory apposition, like the sequence “Abū Ḥafṣ, ʿUmar, al-Fārūq.”
rows.anchor: هما عطف بيان كقوله : سيرة أبي حفص عمر الفاروق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added title King clarifies Lord, since lord can mean owner of a house or goods and can be used of human masters.
rows.anchor: فوصف أولا بأنه رب الناس ثم الرب قد يكون ملكا وقد لا يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added title God clarifies King, since a king need not be divine, whereas God is uniquely His and He has no partner in it.
rows.anchor: ثم الملك قد يكون إلها وقد لا يكون فلا جرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order moves from Lord, who manages and nurtures and gives intellect, to King, whom the servant recognizes himself as belonging to, and then to God, who deserves worship.
rows.anchor: وأيضا بدأ بذكر الرب وهو اسم لمن قام بتدبيره وإصلاحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another progression begins with recognizing God’s visible and hidden favors as Lord, advances to His majesty and self-sufficiency as King, then to His greatness beyond description as God.
rows.anchor: أول ما يعرف العبد من ربه كونه مطيعا لما عنده من النعم الظاهرة والباطنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating “people” supplies the extra clarity explanatory apposition needs and honors people by defining God as their Lord, King, and God; their rank merits this ending to the Book.
rows.anchor: لأن عطف البيان يحتاج إلى مزيد الإظهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says “Owner of people” is not valid here: Lord already means their owner, so King adds a distinct sense; Owner of Judgment Day is allowed in al-Fātiḥa because it refers to another object.
rows.anchor: أفاد كونه مالكا لهم فلا بد وأن يكون المذكور عقيبه هذا الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-Fātiḥa, Lord of the worlds concerns existing things, while Owner of Judgment Day means power over that future day, so the titles are not repetitive.
rows.anchor: وهي الأشياء الموجودة في الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Permitted readings follow transmitted revelation rather than analogy; Mālik was nevertheless read in anomalous readings.
rows.anchor: وأيضا فجواز القراءات يتبع النزول لا القياس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waswās as a noun means whispering, like zalzāl meaning shaking; the verbal noun is waswās with kasra, like zilzāl.
rows.anchor: الوسواس اسم بمعنى الوسوسة ، كالزلزال بمعنى الزلزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term denotes Satan, named as the whispering itself because whispering is his craft and occupation; Rāzī links this construction to “it is an unrighteous deed.”
rows.anchor: والمراد به الشيطان سمي بالمصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says the detailed treatment of whispering was given earlier in the explanation of Satan whispering to the two.
rows.anchor: وتحقيق الكلام في الوسوسة قد تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khannās means one whose habit is retreating, from khunūs meaning withdrawal or delay.
rows.anchor: وأما الخناس فهو الذي عادته أن يخنس منسوب إلى الخنوس وهو التأخر

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says Satan retreats and leaves when a person remembers God, but whispers when the person is heedless.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير إذا ذكر الإنسان ربه خنس الشيطان وولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative pronoun alladhī can be genitive as an adjective, or nominative or accusative as an expression of censure; after khannās a reciter may pause and begin anew with alladhī under either latter parsing.
rows.anchor: يجوز في محله الحركات الثلاث فالجر على الصفة والرفع والنصب على الشتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can mean that the whispering retreating tempter comes from either jinn or humans; a human tempter poses as a concerned adviser, retreats if rebuffed, and intensifies if accepted.
rows.anchor: وكما أن شيطان الجن قد يوسوس تارة ويخنس أخرى فشيطان الإنس يكون كذلك

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some take jinn and humans as two subgroups of the people mentioned in “people’s breasts,” treating insān as both a shared genus and a species.
rows.anchor: قسمان مندرجان تحت قوله في : { صدور الناس } كأن القدر المشترك بين الجن والإنس

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: They cite a report in which a group of jinn called themselves “people from the jinn,” and the Qur’an’s calling jinn “men” as support for calling them people.
rows.anchor: ما روى أنه جاء نفر من الجن فقيل لهم : من أنتم فقالوا : أناس من الجن

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: On this interpretation the persistent whisperer misguides not only humankind but its own kind, the jinn, so sensible people should beware.
rows.anchor: أن هذا الوسواس الخناس شديد الخنث لا يقتصر على إضلال الإنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī calls the genus interpretation weak: linguistically jinn are hidden beings, while insān denotes visibility and perception, so it is remote to make humans a genus including jinn.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول ضعيف ، لأن جعل الإنسان اسما للجنس الذي يندرج فيه الجن والإنس بعيد

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf’s author repairs that interpretation by taking al-nās in “people’s breasts” as al-nāsī, the forgetful; jinn and humans both forget God’s due.
rows.anchor: وقال صاحب الكشاف : من أراد تقرير هذا الوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading coordinates the phrase with the act of seeking refuge: seek refuge from that devil and then from all jinn and humans.
rows.anchor: أن يكون المراد أعوذ برب الناس من الوسواس الخناس ومن الجنة والناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-Falaq the refuge is sought from three kinds of harm under one divine attribute, Lord of daybreak.
rows.anchor: المستعاذ به في السورة الأولى مذكور بصفة واحدة وهي أنه رب الفلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-Nās the refuge is sought from one harm, whispering, under three divine attributes: Lord, King, and God of people.
rows.anchor: وأما في هذه السورة فالمستعاذ به مذكور بصفات ثلاثة : وهي الرب والملك والإله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The praise corresponds to the request: the first sūra seeks bodily and worldly safety, the second the safety of religion, showing even slight harm to religion outweighs immense worldly harm.
rows.anchor: أن الثناء يجب أن يتقدر بقدر المطلوب ، فالمطلوب في السورة الأولى سلامة النفس والبدن
